Ava N.: hey all :wave: first day — quick q about secrets onboarding. I need read-only access to a few project API keys for local dev and also need to be able to decrypt a couple of test blobs with our KMS. what's the fastest way to request that without getting blocked?

Samir R.: welcome Ava! :tada: we use Vault for secret storage and our KMS is backed by cloud KMS. For humans, the usual flow is: 1) request a secrets role via the onboarding portal, 2) request a KMS grant for your service account if you need decrypt. If it's just readonly dev access that's usually day-0.

Ava N.: where's the onboarding portal link? also what info do I need to include in the request so it doesn't get stuck in triage?

Samir R.: portal is https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard (bookmark it). include: project name, env (dev/staging), which exact secrets (names or paths), why you need them, duration (e.g. 30/90 days), and your GitHub/GCP identity. quick example request body I usually paste into the form:```
Project: client-alpha
Environment: dev
Secrets: projects/client-alpha/creds/api_key, projects/client-alpha/kv/db_readonly
Reason: reproduce integration bug and run local tests
Duration: 30 days
GitHub: ava
```
Maria S.: heads up from security: we prefer short-lived access. For KMS decrypt we only grant session-scoped decrypt or require you to run operations from a dev bastion in some cases. Also: never copy secrets into plaintext files on your laptop. Use `vault login` + `vault kv get -field=value` or the secrets helper in the SDKs.

Ava N.: got it — is there a separate approval queue for KMS? who signs off?

Samir R.: KMS is a separate workflow — tag your ticket with `kms-decrypt` and it'll route to Platform Security (usually Maria or Ops to approve). If it's for a temporary dev task we can often do a fast-track approval same day.

ops-bot: Automated: Please attach the minimum required IAM policy and the ticket will be routed. See https://internal.redwood.dev/security/kms-guidelines for policy snippets.

Maria S.: also small note: if you need to rotate keys as part of the work, state that up front. rotations are logged and need a rollback plan. For dev-only keys we usually do a 30d TTL and auto-rotate; production rotation requires a runbook.

Ava N.: awesome thanks — I'll open the portal ticket now with that template. cc @Samir R. if anything weird pops up. :raised_hands:
